text: LLaMA 2 is released as open-source with 70B parameters, licensed for commercial use
LLaMA 2 Chat models trained with RLHF achieve safety improvements and reduced harmful outputs
LLaMA 2 models outperform or match closed-source models like ChatGPT on multiple benchmarks
Vision Transformers (ViT) split images into patches and apply transformer architecture directly
ViT models trained on ImageNet achieve better accuracy than CNN baselines with equivalent compute
QLoRA enables efficient fine-tuning of 65B parameter models on a single 48GB GPU
QLoRA uses 4-bit quantization and LoRA adapters to reduce memory requirements by 5x
Scaling laws show that larger models demonstrate emergent abilities not present in smaller models
Language models exhibit power-law scaling where loss decreases proportionally to model and data size
LLM agents for software engineering can write, test, and debug code with minimal human supervision
Mixtral of Experts model uses selective routing to activate only 2 out of 8 expert modules per token
Mixtral achieves superior performance to Llama 2 70B while using fewer active parameters
Vision transformers with sparse mixture of experts scale to billions of parameters efficiently
GPT-4 exhibits improved reasoning, accuracy, and safety compared to GPT-3.5
GPT-4 shows improved performance across academic and professional exams including law, medicine, and coding
LLaMA foundation models achieve strong performance on academic benchmarks through next-token prediction only
LLaMA 13B outperforms GPT-3 on many NLU and NLG tasks despite having fewer parameters
Mistral 7B language model matches or exceeds Llama 2 13B performance on multiple benchmarks
Mistral uses grouped query attention to reduce memory requirements and increase inference speed
Mistral 7B is released with an Apache 2.0 license allowing commercial and research use
